title: Of Errors and Echoes: Responsibility-Aware Credit Assignment for Tool-Use Agents
abstract: arXiv:2610.16027v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Reinforcement learning improves tool-use agents, yet fine-grained credit assignment remains challenging even with step-level feedback. An observed error may be inherited from an earlier decision, while multiple responsible decisions may share the same downstream consequence or participate in later recovery. We introduce Error-Chain-Aware Optimization (ECHO), a responsibility-aware credit assignment framework that separates responsibility identification from credit allocation. A frozen judge combines retrospective trajectory analysis with decision-time assessment from the policy-visible prefix to distinguish newly introduced errors, inherited consequences, missed corrections, and successful corrections. ECHO then counts shared downstream consequences once across responsible decisions and constrains rewards for repairing self-induced errors through source-funded recovery, producing bounded action-level supervision alongside terminal supe

translated_title: 论错误与回声：面向工具使用智能体的责任感知信用分配
translated_abstract: 强化学习可以提升工具使用智能体的表现，但即使有步级反馈，细粒度的信用分配仍然充满挑战。观察到的错误可能继承自先前的决策，而多个负有责任的决策可能共享相同的下游后果，或参与到后续的修复过程中。我们提出了错误链感知优化（ECHO），这是一个将责任识别与信用分配相分离的责任感知信用分配框架。一个冻结的裁判模型将回溯性轨迹分析与基于策略可见前缀的决策时评估相结合，以区分新引入的错误、继承的后果、错失的修正和成功的修正。随后，ECHO对多个负有责任的决策所共享的下游后果只计数一次，并通过由错误源头出资的修复机制来约束修复自致错误所获得的奖励，从而在终端监督之外生成有界的动作级监督信号。
tldr: 提出ECHO框架，通过区分新引入错误、继承后果与错失或成功的修正，并去重共享后果、约束自致错误修复的奖励，解决了工具使用智能体强化学习中细粒度信用分配的难题。
